Confirm that the final reason’s specific finding actually appears in the report and is not contradicted by a normal statement. Then check polarity: a supported abnormality means answer “No” to “Does this image look normal?”; no supported abnormality means answer “Yes.” Do not rely on a bare tool “Yes”/“No” alone. If options are displayed, also map the supported answer text to the displayed option and verify that the letter and text agree.

In this case, the grounded report explicitly named “A left-sided vascular catheter is present,” and chest_xray_expert answered “No” to “Is this chest X-ray normal?” The terminal “No” and its reason matched that evidence; no option map was present.

Trigger: When finalizing a yes/no answer to an image-normality question after a grounded findings report and/or an expert normal/abnormal answer is available.

Verification action: Read the grounded report and locate at least one explicit abnormal finding for the same image and attribute—e.g., “left-sided vascular catheter is present,” line/tube, infiltrate. Confirm that the final reason’s specific finding actually appears in the report and is not contradicted by a normal statement. Then check polarity: a supported abnormality means answer “No” to “Does this image look normal?”; no supported abnormality means answer “Yes.” Do not rely on a bare tool “Yes”/“No” alone. If options are displayed, also map the supported answer text to the displayed option and verify that the letter and text agree.

In this case, the grounded report explicitly named “A left-sided vascular catheter is present,” and chest_xray_expert answered “No” to “Is this chest X-ray normal?” The terminal “No” and its reason matched that evidence; no option map was present.

Trigger: When finalizing a yes/no answer to an image-normality question after a tool returns only a bare “normal/abnormal” response, especially if the draft reason names specific imaging findings or claims they were confirmed by a grounded report.

Verification action: Check the actual observed tool results for a grounded report on the same image and attribute. For every named finding in the final reason—e.g., “calcified granuloma” or “calcified mediastinal lymph nodes”—confirm that the finding explicitly appears in an observed report or other tool output. If no grounded report was run, or it does not contain the cited finding, do not attribute that finding to the report; either obtain/read the grounded report or limit the reason to the observed bare expert answer. Confirm polarity: a supported abnormality means “No” to “Is this image normal?”, while no supported abnormality means “Yes.” If options are displayed, map the supported answer text to the displayed choice and verify that the letter and text agree.

In this case, the terminal “No” matched the released reference and the expert tool’s bare “No,” but the reason’s specific findings—calcified granuloma and calcified mediastinal lymph nodes—were not present in any observed tool output. The correct grade alone did not validate the rationale; this was an unsupported-reason/evidence error, not an option-mapping error because no options were present.

Trigger: Finalizing a yes/no answer to “Is this image a sagittal plane?” when the rationale describes a frontal/coronal chest view rather than a side view.

Observable verification action: Confirm the rationale bases the answer on orientation landmarks in the current image—e.g., symmetric bilateral lungs, central heart, and clavicles indicate a frontal/coronal chest radiograph, not a sagittal side view—and that the stated answer directly negates the sagittal-plane claim. If answer options are displayed, map the supported “No” text back to the displayed choice and verify the letter and text agree; here no options were present, so no mapping is needed. Do not treat the correct grade alone as proof: the “No” must be supported by the described image orientation, and no unsupported tool finding should be introduced.
